Wrap the executor call and `normalizeToolResponse` in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts:83-92` in a `try/catch`. On catch, log the tool name, `error.name` and the message (truncated to 500 characters, matching the org's existing bound in `cfoagent`'s `gemini.ts`) at `error` level, and return a resolved `ToolResponse` whose `result` is a fixed English sentence naming the tool - never the thrown message itself, since a third-party error string can carry an internal hostname or another customer's identifier and the engine redacts nothing. Handle non-`Error` throws (`throw 'boom'`, `throw undefined`) the same way. Leave `onError` un-fired for a caught throw - the turn now succeeds, so no failure hook runs - and update `docs/tool-responses.md`, `docs/adding-a-tool.md`, `docs/a…

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An end-to-end `chatOrchestrator` test with a throwing executor asserts `processMessage` resolves and the provider's second call receives a `tool_result` block naming the tool
- [ ] The same test asserts `onError` was **not** called while `afterModelResponse` **was** - the turn succeeded
- [ ] `execute` carries JSDoc stating the three-part contract: resolves for a model-caused failure, resolves for an executor throw, throws only for caller-malformed input
- [ ] `docs/tool-responses.md`, `docs/adding-a-tool.md` and `docs/architecture.md` state that a throwing executor is caught, the model is told the call failed, and the thrown message reaches only the log

Part of #56

## Why

`ToolRegistry.execute` awaits the registered executor with no `try`, so whatever it throws rejects one of the promises in `executeToolCalls`'s `Promise.all`, escapes `processMessageStream`, and becomes a `SERVER_ERROR` / "Failed to process message" that ends the customer's whole conversation - taking every other tool result from the same round with it. The docs already tell tool authors not to throw, but nothing enforces it. `079` drew the line for every model-caused failure…

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new test in `chatOrchestrator.test.ts` drives a stub provider yielding a `tool_use` call named `get_bokking_status` then a stop, then plain text on the second round. `processMessage` resolves, and the messages handed to the provider's second call contain a `tool_result` block with `toolUseId: 'tu-1'` whose `content` names `get_bokking_status`
- [ ] A round containing one unknown name and one registered tool returns both results: the registered tool's executor runs exactly once and its result reaches `messages` unchanged (today the unknown name rejects the `Promise.all` and the good result is discarded with it)

# Support agent TMS tools

## User Scenarios & Testing

### User Story 4 - A crashed tool reaches a human and leaks nothing (Priority: P2) (#185)

A tool's executor throws mid-turn. The customer's turn still completes, the model receives a fixed result naming the tool and saying a human has been told, and one audit row and one escalation record exist. The thrown error carries internal detail and the tool input carries customer data; none of it reaches the model, the audit row, the escalation record or the logs, whose one line names the tool and the error's class only (RD-7).

**Why this priority:** It is the callback the client requires, and today it is lost on every crash. Error messages are the most common place an internal hostname or a customer's name escapes.

- [ ] A full turn on the real engine - mock provider emitting one `tool_use` for a tool registered through `registerTools.ts` whose executor throws - completes with a `stream_end`, and the `tool_result` handed to the provider's second call is byte-identical to the guard's constant; the same test asserts one `auditEntries` row and one `escalations` document exist, which the engine's own backstop cannot produce

content.text: {"answer": "The engine-level catch is `ToolRegistry.execute` in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts`. Issue #138 describes wrapping the executor call and `normalizeToolResponse` there in a try/catch. A throw then becomes a resolved `ToolResponse` that names the tool, and `onError` is not fired. Issue #185 separately describes an app-level wrapper, `withCrashGuard(toolName, executor)`, for the support-agent TMS tools. It also catches executor throws, and it records an audit row and an escalation. I only saw the issue and spec text, not the code, so I can't confirm either function is implemented as described.", "sources": ["issue-138 (re-cinq/Otto)", "issue-185 (re-cinq/Otto)", "specs/support-agent-tms-tools/spec.md"]}
